/Issued 1202 AM MDT Sat Aug 29 2026/ 

 - Meteorological Overview:

An active and unsettled pattern will bring daily chances for 
precipitation, with the exception of Monday, to most locations over 
the course of the next week. Over the course of the next week 
temperatures will fluctuate between near to below normal, with the 
coldest day of the upcoming week arriving on Sunday as a large upper 
level trough moves overhead. As this upper level trough and closed 
low moves overhead on Sunday snow levels will fall to as low as 
7000ft across the Glacier National Park region, which could lead to 
some light snow accumulations for the peaks of the park. 
Additionally on Sunday, increasing cross barrier flow will 
contribute to breezy and gusty west winds for most locations across 
Southwest through North Central Montana, especially over the plains 
of Central and North Central Montana. Prior to the trough moving 
overhead on Sunday moist and unstable southwest flow aloft combined 
with sufficient shear will help to support the potential for a few 
strong thunderstorms across Southwest Montana today, generally along 
and south of the I-90 corridor. The main threat from any storm that 
does become strong or severe will be strong winds, especially along 
the immediate Idaho and Wyoming borders.

Beyond the weekend broad troughing continues to be supported across 
the Western CONUS, especially from Tuesday through next Saturday, 
with moist southwest flow over the Northern Rockies helping to 
support the aforementioned daily chances for showers and 
thunderstorms. - MOldan

- Forecast Confidence & Scenarios:

Gusty Winds on Sunday...

ECMWF EFIs continue to support the potential for a climatologically 
unusual, with respect to the final week of August, wind event along 
the Rocky Mountain and across the Montana Hwy 200 corridor on Sunday 
as cross barrier flow increases to between 35-45kts; which is 
generally 1 to 1.5 standard deviations above normal per NAEFS 
analysis. BUFKIT soundings across the aforementioned areas depict 
deep mixing to between 4-6kft during the afternoon hours on Sunday, 
which will coincide with the passage off the upper level trough axis 
and associated subsidence. This gives increased confidence that a 
period of strong and gusty winds will occur, especially across wind 
prone areas of Central and North Central Montana, during the 
afternoon and into the early evening hours. While High Wind 
highlights do not look necessary those traveling along the Rocky 
Mountain Front in high profile vehicles should be prepared for 
periods of strong cross winds.

Weekend Precipitation...

Multiple rounds of showers and isolated thunderstorms will bring 
beneficial rainfall to most of Southwest through North Central 
Montana, with the exception of the the East Glacier Park Region and 
Northern High Plains zones where the probability for wetting (0.1") 
rainfall is largely less than a 50% chance, over the next 48 hours 
(12z Saturday through 12z Monday). Outside of these areas most other 
locations have a 70%+ chance of a wetting rainfall through Sunday 
night, with a corridor of 40-80% chance probabilities for a 0.5" of 
rainfall for areas along and east of a Lewistown, to Great Falls, to 
Townsend, to Bozeman, to Ennis, to Monida Pass line.
